narrative.text:
I’ll first verify the exact base and pinned toolchain before installing dependencies or changing files. This is the narrow dial/two-sink task only; broader diagnostic redaction, catalogue admission, and drift guards remain parked, and this work does not authorize strict-mode rollout.
Preflight passed: exact starting commit and ten-file part-1 diff, Bun 1.4.3 with the expected SHA-256, Node 22.23.3, and npm 10.9.9. The isolated, scripts-disabled install produced the exact supplied lockfile digest and dependency versions; the lockfile bytes are preserved outside the repository.
The unmodified baseline build, typecheck, and Node suite passed: 7,900 tests passed, 45 skipped. Step 0 reproduced structured `response.statusCode` on both engines for 401, 403, 404, 500, and 302; misleading reason phrases and bodies did not change it. Bun’s request has `abort()` but no `destroy()`.

Both sinks leaked the synthetic credential through real failed model turns and the public host-alert route, including all tested encodings and the first credential after 17 rotations. Before production edits, I’m checking a scope issue: configuration-close cleanup and preserving fixed webhook templates appear to require changes outside the two permitted sink sites.
The manager’s answer permits strict-only lifecycle hooks and changes to Step-0-proved alert callers within the same three production files and roughly 300 net lines; removed, closed, or stopped configurations must leave the union, and re-adding the same object must start with an empty accepted set.
The manager narrowed R3 to filtering assembled variable text at the two sink boundaries, with no per-caller template changes: separate fixed fields remain untouched, while template text matching a strict credential is accepted over-redaction that must be documented and tested.
The dial mapping and 32-character minimum are committed locally, with original-base comparisons passing on both engines for omitted, false, and null flags.

The two-sink implementation is now under test. The reproduced leak routes pass absence assertions, including rotation and the tested encodings. The mixed-set probe exercises a real non-strict tool failure and checks removal, closure, and re-adding the same configuration object. No parked diagnostic sink has been changed.
The environment update changes the date to 2026-10-28 UTC; it does not change the task scope or permissions.
The full Node suite passed on the committed candidate: 7,947 passed, 45 skipped, and no failures. Build and typecheck also passed. The isolated Bun baseline had 175 pre-existing failures across 33 files; the final Bun run is underway so I can compare the failure inventories rather than report that suite as green.
I found a compatibility gap in the sink-copy implementation: a native Error supplied as alert data could change formatting even when it contained no credential. I’ll preserve the existing formatting for ordinary Errors while keeping the redacted copy detached, then repeat the comparisons and final gates.
The manager approved cleanup based on an existing strict lifetime record, even if the flag has since become false, and confirmed that both sinks must match the declared already-escaped forms as well as raw text; the template-collision test remains required.
The mixed-mode comparison caught a formatting difference in already-prepared diagnostic data. I corrected it so the two exporting sinks preserve the original formatting apart from credential redaction; the focused tests pass. I’m finishing the end-to-end comparisons and final report.A final lifecycle probe found a gap: if a held non-strict configuration is mutated to strict and dialed directly, its accepted credential does not enter the framework’s union. I’ve asked for a decision because the proposed fix changes the previously approved lifecycle guard. The candidate is not ready to claim complete.The manager requires runtime enabling to join the union, preferably through lazy accepted sets, and permits inert ownership bookkeeping if needed; I’ll preserve independent framework lifetimes and rerun both-engine legacy comparisons.The runtime-enabling fix passes on both engines: ownership records remain inert until a strict dial accepts a credential, and separate frameworks retain independent lifetimes. The amended local commit is `aed092aa`; clean build, suite and compatibility checks are running again before finalization.The final Node suite, build, typecheck, both-engine legacy/mixed-mode comparisons and 272-cell sink checks pass. The isolated Bun suite is finishing its known failing baseline cases; I’ll report those failures separately rather than call that suite green.Verification is complete. The final candidate has no new Bun failures, and the legacy/mixed-mode comparisons and sink checks pass on both engines. The report and unpublished PR draft are in the evidence directory; I’m finalizing the local implementation now.The queued manager messages require four changes: retain redaction through reconnects and flag-off transitions until lifetime end, distinguish pre-flip legacy credentials, document the shared-object behavior, and verify both writer boundaries; they also confirm the fragment refusal is an unchanged admission case, not a constructor test. I’ll add that evidence and use the required wording, “assembled-text redaction at the sink boundary, by manager decision.”The follow-up checks now pass on both engines: credentials remain redacted while reconnect is pending, after reconnect, and while the flag is off; pre-flip legacy credentials remain raw. The source audit found one failures.log writer and one ops-webhook sender. The amended candidate is `d2b5fbf0`, with final clean gates running again.
